t: British troops captured Fort Peter in St. Marys, in the only battle of the War of 1812 to take place in the state of Georgia.
War of 1812: The American frigate USS President, commanded by Commodore Stephen Decatur, was captured by a squadron of four British frigates.
The United States ratifies the Treaty of Ghent – signed in late 1814 – formally ending the War of 1812.
Napoleon escaped from the Italian island of Elba, to which he had been exiled after the signing of the Treaty of Fontainebleau.
Joachim Murat, King of Naples, issued the Rimini Proclamation, among the earliest calls for Italian unification.
Mount Tambora in Indonesia began the most powerful volcanic eruption in recorded history, killing at least 71,000 people and affecting temperatures worldwide.
War of the Seventh Coalition: Napoleon fought and lost his final battle, the Battle of Waterloo, in present-day Belgium.
Aboard HMS Bellerophon, French emperor Napoleon surrendered to Royal Navy captain Frederick Lewis Maitland, concluding the Napoleonic Wars.
Napoleon began his exile on Saint Helena in the South Atlantic Ocean, which would encompass his final six years.
Jane Austen's novel Emma was first published, the last novel released during her lifetime.
